title: Dependency catalogue with sticky acceptance criteria and handoff checklist
creator: Maya Alvarez
description:
Problem: Roadmap handoffs frequently surface late-stage integration assumptions (API surface, auth, infra quotas) that delay releases by 1-3 sprints. Current dependency lists are brittle: owners change, acceptance criteria are implicit, and follow-up tasks are not stickied to the upstream ticket.

Proposal: Create a lightweight, human-readable dependency catalogue and 'sticky acceptance criteria' pattern attached to initiative-level tickets. The catalogue will: 1) enumerate required outputs by team (API contracts, schema versions, infra capacity, design sign-off); 2) include explicit acceptance criteria per output; 3) attach a one-click handoff checklist that creates assigned follow-up tasks in target team queues (ENG/DES/SEC/INFRA).

Scope: Pilot for three initiatives in Q2 (Console rollout, Dedicated autoscaling UI, Private deployment KMS integration). Deliverables: a dependency catalogue template, a set of acceptance-criteria templates, a minimal UI flow in the Roadmap tool for creating handoff checklists, and a PM-run playbook for onboarding partner teams.

Why this matters: Makes implicit dependencies explicit and measurable, reduces last-minute escalations, improves on-time delivery for cross-functional initiatives, and provides material signals for OKR progress reporting.
acceptance_criteria: Dependency catalogue template stored in Confluence with examples for Console/Dedicated/Private initiatives
One-click handoff checklist prototype that creates follow-up Linear tickets in partner teams with prefilled acceptance criteria
All pilot initiatives have at least one documented dependency with owner and acceptance criteria before kickoff (definition of ready)
PMs confirm handoff checklist reduced unplanned cross-team follow-ups in pilot by >=30% (preliminary survey)
success_metrics: % initiatives with documented dependencies at kickoff >= 90% for pilot cohort
Reduction in cross-team unplanned blockers per initiative >= 30%
Median days between blocker discovery and resolution reduced from baseline by 25%
Time-to-close for created follow-up tickets <= 7 days for low-complexity items
rollout_plan: Week 1: Draft templates and internal review with ENG/DES/SEC/INFRA leads
Week 2: Build a minimal handoff checklist generator (no deep UI — uses Linear API + template payloads) and test on 1 initiative
Week 3: Run pilot across 3 initiatives, collect feedback, update templates
Week 4: Iterate and produce PM playbook + training session for cross-functional leads; plan wider rollout next cycle
risks: Teams may view handoff checklist as additional process overhead; mitigate by keeping templates minimal and automating ticket creation
Linear API rate/permission limits could block automated handoff creation for some teams; engineering dependency ENG-1842 is on the critical path
Security review for Private/KMS work may add nondeterministic delays; coordinate with SEC-501 early
open_questions: Should acceptance criteria live on the initiative ticket or be owned per sub-issue? (trade-off: discoverability vs. duplication)
Do we need integration with Console dashboards to surface unresolved dependencies to execs?
What SLAs should be attached to follow-up tickets created by the checklist?
